rationale: This 1950 law review article examines doctrinal legal implications of the Central Valley Project—a basin-scale water resource development and land-reclamation/irrigation project in California—drawing on United States v. Gerlach Live Stock Co. It fails Criterion 1 (wrong service: basin water resource development and land irrigation rather than household or community water/sanitation service access), Criterion 3 (pure doctrinal legal commentary with no empirical primary evidence or systematic synthesis), and Criterion 4 (no household/community water or sanitation access outcomes).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording, the article addresses legal factors ('the legal implications of the Central Valley Project'), whereas under the narrow reading it does not examine a legal/administrative mechanism governing household or community water/sanitation service access. Both readings result in exclusion because the article concerns basin-scale agricultural land reclamation/resource development (failing C1) and is a doctrinal legal essay with no empirical evidence (failing C3 and C4).
